Local metaplectic character identity needs packet, transfer and normalization data. A formula in small rank is a parameter instance, not a full identity. AIM parked.

Ratios of unspecified L-function families and moment orders are a research program. A single finite-field identity is not full scope; AIM parked.

The high-dimensional Busemann-difference limit depends on passage-time distribution and almost-sure quantifiers absent here. Deterministic equal weights give a misleading wording counterexample; AIM parked.

Two topological-concordance assertions require a uniform infection invariant. Smooth obstructions do not resolve topological equivalence, and one knot calculation does not settle all homotopic infection curves; AIM parked.

A pro-p identity for the entire positive-characteristic polynomial automorphism congruence group needs a precise completed-word convention. Residual p alone neither implies nor refutes an identity. Kourovka route parked.

Existence of purely pseudo-Anosov surface subgroups and hyperbolic surface-by-surface four-manifolds is a global geometric construction problem. Free Schottky examples and negatively curved analogies do not meet either requested existence scope.

Need a finitely generated free purely pseudo-Anosov subgroup failing convex cocompactness. Individual pseudo-Anosov elements do not certify the all-words condition or non-Schottky property; no bounded certificate route.

Both a free non-Schottky purely irreducible subgroup and nonfree purely irreducible subgroup question are present. Individual fully irreducible generators do not control arbitrary products; large dynamical dependencies.

The non-virtually-cyclic Cayley percolation threshold assertion has a strong known-theorem risk (pc<1 literature). An isoperimetric proof for polynomial growth or nonamenability alone misses intermediate growth; do not promote without the full published theorem body.

Continuity on the transient k-regular Cayley-graph locus needs uniformly small return-probability tails; local convergence controls each finite-time return only. No uniform tail bound or concrete counterexample family established.
Reasonable growth conditions on W must be recovered before a weak Euler-Lagrange claim is well posed. Differentiating energy under arbitrary variations ignores determinant blow-up and admissibility.
A uniform positive Jacobian lower bound for energy minimizers is much stronger than positivity almost everywhere. Coercivity or finite energy alone cannot provide the requested essential lower bound.
Strict polyconvexity is convexity in minors, not strict convexity in deformation gradients. A convex-energy uniqueness argument does not extend to all smooth equilibria in ball-like bodies.

Verified Hayman v1 lines7353-7362 give the precise statement and explicitly report Krushkal [498] proved it. Similarity conjugation F(rz)/r also suggests a routine route under the literal extension definition. Cited proof body and complete dependencies unread; no discovery credit.

Verified Hayman v1 lines8406-8418 explicitly report solutions and reproduction of Ortel's proof by Cantarella et al. This is an existing-proof objection independent of the open metadata; successor body coverage is separately logged.

Latała-van Handel-Youssef dimension-free Gaussian matrix theorem is the direct published-resolution lead. The centered-entry hypothesis must be reconciled with the primary question; no novelty inferred for a noncentered wording variant. Actual theorem-body coverage separately logged.

R_A and its rate and rounding conventions are undefined in the record. An asymptotic Boolean classification identity cannot be checked or refuted by plugging arbitrary interpretations of its three arguments.

Closed form and irrationality of the totient generating value are distinct demands. Möbius inversion gives a convergent Lambert-type series, not irrationality or the desired closed form. Numerical digits would not decide either.

Equivalence of bounded backward heat nonuniqueness and Gaussian harmonic decay depends on boundary data conventions. On bounded domains the growth condition is vacuous; exploiting omitted lateral conditions would be a wording correction, not the intended PDE result.

Existence of a surjective CA with nu(f,S_N)<N depends on the asymptotic jointly-periodic growth definition. A finite list of periodic configurations or shift examples does not certify the strict asymptotic deficit.

An explicit fast-growing universally good sequence must give recurrence and convergence for powers and commuting transformations. Diagonal existence of an unspecified subsequence does not supply explicitness or simultaneous full scope.
Almost every convex polygon is a measure-theoretic family assertion. One unbounded kite or finite orbit experiment is insufficient; renormalization/parameter control is substantial.

Boundary extension obstruction for every nonmonomial degree n>2 Blaschke product requires global mating-boundary control. Monomial conjugacy and boundary-identification conventions need primary definitions before any literal exception claim.

A common immediate-basin intersection over all 0<h<=m is stronger than individual Newton access channels. Estimates for h=m or one polynomial do not yield a uniform absolute constant over d and all roots.

Four successively restricted Kelvin optimality assertions are requested. Weaire-Phelan comparisons do not automatically respect fundamental-domain, congruent-cell or equal-pressure constraints; no compatible exact competitor certified.

A universal directional shear-modulus bound for arbitrary unit-average-area planar froths needs a mechanical definition and admissibility constraints. Honeycomb perimeter optimality is not a shear-modulus theorem.

The tensor identities define finite-dimensional linear constraints, suggesting Young-symmetry decomposition rather than a search. But investigating structure is not a single new theorem, and standard affine-curvature-module classifications are a decisive routine-adaptation risk. No source body or eligible classification established.

The leading smaller-m question refers to an omitted construction; even the quaternionic subproblem requires normalization and local-closeness topology. No credit for low-dimensional degeneracy or notation correction.

A local period-map diffeomorphism does not imply global injectivity; holonomy G2 metrics across an entire compact seven-manifold moduli component require global geometric control. No short certificate or obstruction established.

Effective minimal biLipschitz area/length-extremality constants require precise extremality and curvature hypotheses; the OCR-like literal text does not provide them. A coarse pinching estimate would not evaluate the minimum.
The literal row omits the graph and Problem7 needed to define the strata. No Cayley-algebra calculation is meaningful until those objects are recovered; do not invent a replacement graph.

All closed spatial curves at fixed length require a convex-hull surface-area bound with double-covered planar disks. Planar isoperimetry alone misses spatial hulls; tetrahedral tests would be parameter checks only.

All compact embedded one-sided CMC surfaces with convex planar boundary require a topology theorem, not just spherical-cap uniqueness. Alexandrov reflection needs additional boundary control; no full mechanism established.

The problem first asks for a meaning of exact energy determination; no fixed allowed function or algorithm class is specified. An impossibility statement cannot follow from numerical nonintegrability or lack of a hydrogen-like formula.
Uniform bounded excess electron number as Z grows is the full Coulomb ionization problem. Bounds linear or sublinear in Z, or Hartree-Fock/Thomas-Fermi analogues, do not settle this Hamiltonian.

An alternative proof and Gaussian-integer interpretation require the exact paper's identities and f(a,b,c,d). These objects are omitted from the literal statement. Reproving an already established identity alone earns no discovery credit.

Both flip and branch-rotation chains require O(n^(3/2)) relaxation bounds with the source transition normalization. A coupling bound with extra logarithms or only one chain is incomplete; no bounded exact certificate route.
